entries.test: Whether large language models released after June 2022 showed measurable capability gains over GPT-3-era models on standard benchmarks.
entries.note: This is a modest concession, responding to Alexander's first bet. 'Headroom' implies further gains, so it reads close to a forecast.

entries.test: Whether the BIG-bench paper (Srivastava et al., 2022) reports that performance improved with scale on some tasks but not on others.
entries.note: The 'wall' label is Marcus's own framing. The checkable part is what the paper reports.
This is a research-direction recommendation, drawn from the BIG-bench conclusion he quotes.

entries.test: Whether the first system widely accepted as AGI relies centrally on large-scale symbolic knowledge.
entries.note: Both 'AGI' and 'crucial' are loosely defined. It can only be settled once a system widely accepted as AGI exists.

entries.test: Whether the first system widely accepted as AGI uses explicit cognitive models as a central component.
entries.note: 'Explicit cognitive models' is vague, but there is a plain architectural reading.

entries.test: Whether the first system widely accepted as AGI relies centrally on explicit operations over variables (storing, retrieving and comparing values).
entries.note: Can only be settled once a system widely accepted as AGI exists.

entries.test: Whether the first system widely accepted as AGI implements an explicit type/token distinction as a central mechanism.
entries.note: Can only be settled once a system widely accepted as AGI exists.

The proposition describes what he did (added an item to a list) rather than what he commits to: that this capacity is an unsolved challenge needing new concepts. It is not a forecast, and what 'reaching' this capacity means has no shared test.

entries.test: Whether a pure CNN/RNN/Transformer system with no writable discrete memory passes a fair implementation of Marcus's Comprehension Challenge (answering open-ended questions about novels and films).
entries.note: 'I think' plus 'stand by' reads as a firm expectation. He also promised a YouTube video admitting error if a scaled-up GPT passes.
